title: Choose the Ad Radar working surface
question: All three keep Frank's existing visual language and the same Hermes lifecycle. Choose which daily job should dominate the app.

options.label: Observation Timeline
options.thesis: Make change over time the primary navigation, so every new, changed, stopped, quarantined, approved, or published creative lands as a precise observation.
options.viewport: A compact run and freshness header sits above a full-height observation rail; the selected event opens its creative, source, classification, media QA, and receipt evidence in a fixed inspector.
options.risk: High-volume runs can bury deliberate comparison unless the compare tray and saved filters remain pinned.

options.label: Creative Fieldbook
options.thesis: Put the searchable creative library first, with evidence-rich cards and a persistent tray for comparing ads across advertisers, locations, formats, hooks, and time.
options.viewport: A terse search and filter ledger spans the top, a dense creative contact sheet fills the workspace, and a right inspector plus bottom compare tray expose evidence without leaving the library.
options.risk: A library-first surface can make runtime failures feel secondary unless live health and attention states stay visible.

options.label: Signal Desk
options.thesis: Unify research setup, live findings, and evidence in one three-pane operator desk with the current Hermes stage always visible.
options.viewport: A narrow sources and research-brief pane feeds a central live creative stream; a fixed evidence inspector closes the loop while a top stage ribbon exposes run, pause, retry, quarantine, and approval state.
options.risk: The simultaneous context is powerful but can become dense below laptop width unless panes collapse with discipline.
